interview_parallel: Sprinklr / Meesho data-science senior round — take-home design: write the prompt that gets an LLM to produce a churn training pipeline with zero temporal leakage, the single most common way DS take-homes fail review
brief:
You are building a monthly customer-churn model. The hard part is not the estimator — it is avoiding leakage, which is subtle and silently inflates offline metrics that then collapse in production. You need an LLM to generate `train_churn.py` that is correct on the TIME dimension.

The data is one row per (customer_id, snapshot_month) with engineered features and a `churned_next_month` target. The generated script must:

**Time-based split:** train on the earliest 70% of months, test on the latest 30% — a temporal cut on a month boundary, never a random `train_test_split`, with an assertion that all train months precede all test months.

**Fit-on-train-only preprocessing:** any transformer that learns statistics (scaler, imputer, encoder, PCA) is fit on the training fold ONLY and applied to test — enforced structurally with an sklearn `Pipeline`, not fit on the full dataset.

**No target leakage in features:** an explicit allow-list of feature columns (never "all columns except the target"), excluding anything only knowable after the target month.

**Time-respecting validation:** `TimeSeriesSplit`, not `KFold`, for any CV/search.

**Honest evaluation:** ROC-AUC and PR-AUC on the temporal test set, PR-AUC primary because churn is imbalanced, plus a printed leakage self-check.

**Your task:** Write the prompt you would send to an LLM to generate this pipeline. You are NOT writing the pipeline — you are writing the instruction, precise enough that the result would survive a senior DS review for leakage.
acceptance_criteria: Prompt requires a temporal (time-ordered) train/test split on a month boundary and forbids random train_test_split, with an assertion that train months precede test months
Prompt requires preprocessing (scaler/imputer/encoder) to be fit on the training fold ONLY, enforced via an sklearn Pipeline rather than fit on the full dataset
Prompt requires an explicit feature allow-list and calls out excluding columns only knowable after the target month (target leakage)
Prompt requires TimeSeriesSplit (not KFold) for any cross-validation or hyperparameter search
Prompt requires PR-AUC as the primary metric (churn is imbalanced) alongside ROC-AUC on a held-out temporal test set

files.content:
Using Python with pandas and scikit-learn, generate a single, runnable training script `train_churn.py` for a monthly customer-churn model. Correctness on the time dimension matters more than model accuracy — a leaky pipeline is worse than useless.

=== DATA ===
- Input: a DataFrame `df` with one row per (customer_id, snapshot_month) and columns: `customer_id`, `snapshot_month` (datetime, monthly), engineered features, and `churned_next_month` (0/1 target). Assume df is already loaded.

=== 1. TIME-BASED SPLIT (NO SHUFFLE) ===
- Split TEMPORALLY, never randomly: train on the earliest 70% of snapshot_month values, test on the latest 30%. A random train_test_split leaks the future into the past. Sort by snapshot_month and cut on a month boundary so no single month straddles the split.
- Assert that max(train.snapshot_month) < min(test.snapshot_month) and print both boundaries.

=== 2. FIT PREPROCESSING ON TRAIN ONLY ===
- Any transformer that learns statistics (StandardScaler, imputers, target/category encoders, PCA) MUST be fit on the training fold ONLY and then applied to test. Do NOT fit on the full dataset. Build this as an sklearn `Pipeline` (or ColumnTransformer + Pipeline) so fit/transform boundaries are enforced structurally — fit(X_train) then transform(X_test).

=== 3. NO TARGET LEAKAGE IN FEATURES ===
- Explicitly exclude any column that is derived from, or only knowable after, the target month (e.g. `cancelled_date`, `refund_after_churn`, next-month aggregates). List the feature columns by an allow-list, never "all columns except the target", so a leaky column cannot sneak in silently.

=== 4. VALIDATION THAT RESPECTS TIME ===
- For any cross-validation or hyperparameter search, use `TimeSeriesSplit` (expanding window), NOT KFold. Each validation fold must be strictly later than its training fold.

=== 5. HONEST EVALUATION ===
- Report ROC-AUC and PR-AUC (average_precision) on the held-out temporal test set. Because churn is imbalanced, also report the positive rate and treat PR-AUC as the primary metric.
- Print a one-line leakage self-check summarising: split boundaries, that the scaler was fit on train only, and the feature allow-list used.

=== OUTPUT ===
Return the full `train_churn.py`. Use a fixed random_state where randomness remains (e.g. the estimator). Keep it a single readable script with functions: `temporal_split(df)`, `build_pipeline(feature_cols)`, `evaluate(pipe, X_test, y_test)`, and `main(df)`.

seeded_mistakes.bug_description: Prompt says "split the data into train and test" without specifying a TIME-based split, so the LLM uses train_test_split(shuffle=True) — future rows leak into the training fold and offline AUC is wildly optimistic versus production.
seeded_mistakes.why_compass_might_suggest_it: train_test_split is the canonical sklearn idiom the model has seen thousands of times; without an explicit temporal constraint it defaults to random shuffling.
detection_signals: Generated script calls train_test_split without shuffle=False and without a date cut

seeded_mistakes.bug_description: Prompt asks to "scale the features" but does not specify fit-on-train-only, so the LLM calls scaler.fit_transform(X) on the FULL dataset before splitting — the test fold's statistics leak into training via the shared scaler.
seeded_mistakes.why_compass_might_suggest_it: Scaling the whole dataset up front is the pattern in most tutorial notebooks; the fit/transform boundary is a discipline that must be requested explicitly or wrapped in a Pipeline.
detection_signals: Prompt does not mention "fit on train only" or "Pipeline"
Generated script fits the scaler before the split, or on the concatenated X

seeded_mistakes.bug_description: Prompt defines features as "all columns except the target" rather than an allow-list, so a post-outcome column (e.g. cancelled_date, refund_after_churn) is silently included and the model learns to "predict" churn from a consequence of churn.
seeded_mistakes.why_compass_might_suggest_it: "Everything except y" is the least-effort feature selection and reads as reasonable; the model has no way to know which columns are post-target without being told to allow-list.
detection_signals: Prompt does not require an explicit feature allow-list
Prompt has no instruction to exclude columns only knowable after the target month

rubric_anchors.check: Prompt mandates a temporal split (earliest 70% train / latest 30% test on a month boundary) and forbids random splitting, with an assertion that train months precede test months
Prompt requires fit-on-train-only preprocessing via an sklearn Pipeline AND an explicit feature allow-list that excludes post-target columns — the two leakage vectors
Prompt requires TimeSeriesSplit for CV and a printed leakage self-check (split boundaries, scaler-fit scope, allow-list) so leakage is auditable
Prompt requires PR-AUC as the primary metric given class imbalance, reported on a held-out temporal test set alongside ROC-AUC

good_prompts_look_like: Says "split temporally on snapshot_month, earliest 70% train / latest 30% test — never train_test_split with shuffle" and asks for an assertion that all train months precede all test months
Requires "fit every learned transformer on the training fold only, enforced with an sklearn Pipeline" instead of scaling the full dataset
Demands an explicit feature allow-list and names example post-target columns to exclude
Specifies TimeSeriesSplit for CV and PR-AUC as the primary imbalanced-class metric
common_verification_traps: Trusting a high offline ROC-AUC without checking HOW the split was made — a leaky split produces beautiful, meaningless numbers
Checking that a scaler is used but not WHERE it was fit — fit_transform on the full X leaks silently
Reviewing the model code but not the feature list, so a post-outcome column passes unnoticed
